claims.claim: Jabil Inc. identity and NYSE tradability are validated by current Workgraph identity data; cited operating evidence originates from Jabil investor relations and current valuation evidence from StockAnalysis.
Five unique issuer-origin records remain after duplicate-origin collapse in the cumulative packet; current market evidence is independently originated and dated September 23, 2026.

provenance.freshness: current operating evidence through 2026-06-17; market evidence through 2026-09-23; next issuer checkpoint 2026-09-30
provenance.rawVsDerived: consistent with packet identity, Q3 operating claims and current market snapshot

unknowns.unknown: FY2026 Q4 results are scheduled for September 30 and are not yet available.

claims.claim: Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was $8.8B, core operating income $504M and core diluted EPS $3.16; management raised FY2026 outlook to $35B revenue, 5.8% core operating margin, $12.70 core EPS and more than $1.4B adjusted free cash flow.
AI infrastructure demand was described as extremely strong while Automotive and Connected Living improved; power, thermal and rack capability expansion broadens the addressable infrastructure stack.

At September 23, 2026 the shares closed at $308.75 with about $32.35B market capitalization, 38.59 trailing P/E and 19.54 forward P/E; valuation is therefore not treated as exceptionally cheap despite growth.

thesisQuality.basis: Strong AI-infrastructure demand plus expansion into power/thermal/rack capabilities supports durable demand and differentiation, but customer concentration and contract economics limit an exceptional band.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q3 exceeded expectations and FY26 guidance rose to $35B revenue, 5.8% core margin, $12.70 core EPS and >$1.4B adjusted FCF.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Current market snapshot shows $32.35B market cap and 19.54 forward P/E: plausible growth-adjusted upside, but not rare valuation asymmetry.

catalystScore.basis: September 30 FY2026 results are a dated near-term verification event following raised guidance; Adani and capability expansion add medium-term catalysts with execution uncertainty.

governancePower.basis: Management has repeatedly raised outlook while emphasizing profitable growth, capital efficiency and shareholder value; acquisition/alliance execution remains to be proven.

alignment2036.basis: Power, thermal, networking, rack manufacturing and integration are durable physical requirements of dense AI/data-center infrastructure and span multiple geographies.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: AI infrastructure growth coexists with improving Automotive and Connected Living, while manufacturing/engineering capabilities are reusable across end markets.

bottleneckControl.basis: Jabil participates in constrained power, thermal and rack deployment layers, but does not demonstrate sole control or absence of alternative suppliers.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Diversified end markets and architecture-agnostic manufacturing provide multiple demand paths, tempered by hyperscaler capex and large-customer sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.basis: Qualification, manufacturing integration and broader power/thermal capability create switching friction, but customers can redesign, dual-source or vertically integrate.

supplyChainResilience.basis: U.S. manufacturing investment and proposed India capacity improve geographic optionality, while packet risk evidence still identifies critical-component supplier dependence.

pricingPower.basis: Raised 5.8% core operating-margin outlook and strong demand support some economic capture, but manufacturing remains competitive and direct price-pass-through evidence is limited.

riskEvidence.basis: Material but non-gating risks include customer and supplier concentration, hyperscaler capex cyclicality, acquisition/alliance execution and possible customer vertical integration.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity/tradability and operating claims have current primary lineage; valuation has a current independent market source. Confidence is reduced for undisclosed customer-level AI concentration, alliance economics and pending Q4 results.

scoreRecord.thesis: Jabil combines diversified manufacturing scale with expanding power, thermal and rack-integration capability positioned in physical AI-infrastructure constraints; current operating momentum is strong, but value capture remains exposed to customer concentration and competitive manufacturing economics.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A hyperscaler capex slowdown, customer redesign/vertical integration, or weak acquisition/alliance execution could compress growth and margins despite continued AI infrastructure buildout.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Fiscal Q4/FY2026 earnings and fiscal 2027 priorities scheduled for September 30, 2026.

risks.risk: Customer/supplier concentration and hyperscaler capex cyclicality can create sharp demand swings.
Acquisition and proposed alliance economics may not earn expected returns.

unknowns.unknown: Customer-level AI revenue concentration and binding Adani economics are not disclosed in cited evidence.
FY2026 Q4 results remain pending until September 30.
